judge_assessment.explanation: The verdict is right and every relation the judge reports is right, but three of the ten values it says it 'independently counted' do not match the artifact. Counting the symbols in worksheet.tex: problem 5 is Jar A = full ten-frame + 2 loose = 12 against Jar B = full ten-frame + 5 loose = 15, so the comparison is 12 < 15 — the judge wrote '12<16'. Problem 7 is Ada 6 + 7 = 13 against Leo 9 + 3 = 12, so 13 > 12 — the judge wrote '13>10'. Problem 10 is Tray A = ten-frame + 3 = 13 against Tray B = 9 + 5 = 14, so 13 < 14 — the judge wrote '8<9'. verify.json (values ['10+2','10+5'], ['6+7','9+3'], ['10+3','9+5']) and the answer key's worked solutions both agree with my counts, so the artifacts are correct and the verdict text is not. The remaining seven recitations (8, 14, 8>6, difference 3, difference 5, 12=12, difference 6) are exact. Separately, the judge's artifact_findings do not mention that the answer key's Quick Answers bank prints an em dash for five of the ten problems — every compare item (3, 5, 7, 8, 10) — even though all five are verified relations and this key has no manual items.

strengths_to_preserve: Problem 10 is a real synthesis challenge rather than a bigger version of problem 1: Tray A shows a full ten-frame plus 3 and Tray B shows a loose row of 9 plus 5, so the tray that LOOKS structured (13) is the smaller set (14). The worksheet names the trap in the stem ('Tray A starts from a full frame, so it looks like the winner') and the key closes on it ('the tray with the fuller frame is the smaller set. This is the strongest evidence on the page that counting on beats looking').

Problem 8 forces the equals sign by drawing two sets in different shapes (8+4 against 10+2) that count the same, and the key defends it explicitly: 'Being willing to write the equals sign here is real understanding, not a lucky guess.' Interleaved sets usually skip '=' entirely.

The three facets (count-on-to-total, compare-two-sets, how-many-more) are declared in verify.json and genuinely interleaved after the two warm-ups — the order runs total, total, compare, difference, compare, difference, compare, compare, difference, compare — so method choice really is required from problem 3 onward, which is what the prompt asked for.

root_causes.description: Half of this key's Quick Answers bank is blank because render_quick_answers._fmt cannot format a relation. Problems 3, 5, 7, 8 and 10 are all type 'compare' with order 'relation' and verified expecteds '>', '<', '>', '=', '<'; sympify rejects each string and _fmt falls through to '---'. There is no manual item on this sheet, so every dash in the bank is a false blank, and the density here (5 of 10 rows) makes the bank close to useless for its stated purpose.
evidence: evals/runs/curriculum-shardX-20260803T181926Z/tasks/curr-005/verify.json ids 3, 5, 7, 8, 10 are type 'compare', order 'relation', expected '>', '<', '>', '=', '<'; no problem on the sheet is type 'manual'.
The same key's worked solutions print the relations correctly ('Mia's stickers > Ben's stickers', 'Jar A < Jar B', 'Box 1 = Box 2', 'Tray A < Tray B'), so the loss is specific to the bank renderer.

root_causes.description: final_response.md states the worksheet 'runs five pages'; the delivered worksheet.pdf is six pages (pdfinfo, and the machine observation records worksheet_pages 6). The page count is written from the author's expectation rather than read back from the compiled PDF, so a claim about the artifact can drift from the artifact without any gate noticing.
evidence: evals/runs/curriculum-shardX-20260803T181926Z/tasks/curr-005/final_response.md: 'Each problem gets 4–5.5 cm of blank space under the picture plus its own answer line, which is why the sheet runs five pages.'
pdfinfo on evals/runs/curriculum-shardX-20260803T181926Z/tasks/curr-005/worksheet.pdf reports Pages: 6; the packet's machine_observation records worksheet_pages 6.
The other nine cases in this batch state page counts that do match their PDFs, so this is drift rather than a systematic miscount.

improvements.title: Quick Answers must typeset a verified relation instead of the manual-only em dash
improvements.proposed_change: In scripts/render_quick_answers.py, handle relation expecteds before the sympify fallback in _fmt: when a problem entry is type 'compare' with order 'relation', map the expected string '<', '>', '=', '<=', '>=', '!=' onto its LaTeX glyph ($<$, $>$, $=$, $\le$, $\ge$, $\ne$) and, where the compare 'values' are literals, print the resolved comparison (e.g. '$12 < 15$') so the bank row carries the same information as the worked solution. Reserve '---' exclusively for problems whose only entries are type 'manual', and add a build warning when _fmt would emit '---' for a non-manual entry, so a future silent drop is loud. Keep this fix separate from the sympify-sandbox fix (quick-answers-must-not-typeset-python-builtins) — that one must REJECT a non-mathematical object, this one must RENDER a relation.
improvements.regression_test: Add to tests/test_render_quick_answers.py a fixture verify JSON holding one {'id':1,'type':'compare','order':'relation','expected':'<'} entry and one {'id':2,'type':'manual','desc':...} entry, then assert the generated bank contains a typeset '<' on row 1 and '---' on row 2, and that row 1 is not '---'. Today row 1 renders '---' (sympify('<') raises SympifyError and _fmt falls through), so the assertion fails before the fix and passes after. Cases in this run that the test reproduces: curr-005 problems 3, 5, 7, 8 and 10 — five of ten bank rows.
improvements.expected_impact: Every verified inequality/equality answer becomes visible in the answer key's fast-checking bank, and the em dash regains its single meaning ('nobody machine-checked this'), so a grader can tell a verified relation from a genuine manual item at a glance.
improvements.risk: Low. The change is confined to formatting one expected value; existing numeric, list and dict rows are untouched. The only visible difference is that rows previously blank now print a glyph, which can widen a bank column and re-flow column_count — worth asserting the column arithmetic in the same test.

improvements.title: Read page counts back from the compiled PDFs before writing final_response.md
improvements.proposed_change: scripts/build.sh already compiles all three documents and reads the page count from the engine log for the study guide's 2-page cap. Print the final page count of each of the three PDFs in the build summary next to the emitted paths, and instruct in SKILL.md that any page count quoted in the delivery message must be copied from that line rather than estimated. Optionally add a light checker that parses '<n> pages' claims out of final_response.md and compares them against pdfinfo, reported as a warning.
improvements.regression_test: Given a final_response.md claiming 'five pages' and a 6-page worksheet.pdf, assert the checker reports the mismatch naming both numbers; with the claim corrected to 'six pages', assert it is silent. Nothing checks this today, so the first assertion fails before the fix and passes after.
improvements.expected_impact: The delivery message stops making small false statements about the artifacts it is describing, which is the same trust surface as the answer-key claims — cheap to hold correct once the build prints the number.
improvements.risk: Very low. It is a reporting change; the worst case is a noisy warning when a page count is written in words ('five') rather than digits, which the parser should handle for the small number words.

case_summary: A strong interleaved-synthesis sheet for K/1 and a correct ACCEPT. Ten problems, three declared facets genuinely interleaved after two warm-ups, every count re-derived by hand from worksheet.tex and matching verify.json and the key: 8, 14, 8>6, 3, 12<15, 5, 13>12, 12=12, 6, 13<14. The final two items are the best of the set — an '=' answer built from two differently-shaped equal sets, and a challenge where the tray with the full ten-frame is the smaller one. Two findings. First, the judge's own recitation is wrong on three items (it reports 12<16, 13>10 and 8<9 where the artifacts show 12<15, 13>12 and 13<14); the relations are right, so the verdict stands, but its 'independently counted' claim does not survive checking. Second, the answer key's Quick Answers bank prints an em dash for all five verified relation answers, which is half the bank and the same glyph reserved for unchecked manual items. A minor third: final_response.md says the worksheet runs five pages; it runs six.
